trial_name.text: Study LUM001-304 (the pivotal trial supporting approval)

citations.quote: One multicenter adequate and placebo-controlled randomized withdrawal study of maralixibat, Study LUM001-304, showed a direct measurement of benefit for treatment of pruritus in patients with ALGS.
LUM001-304 (NCT02160782)	Pediatric patients with ALGS	Open-label run-in with 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized withdrawal (RWD) period
Study LUM001-304 was designed as a Phase 2 study and enrolled 31 patients with ALGS in an open-label study with a 4-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal period (RWD).

design.text: Open-label run-in with a 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized withdrawal (RWD) period; the FDA focused on the 4-week RWD period comparing patients remaining on maralixibat with those switched to placebo.

citations.quote: LUM001-304 (NCT02160782)	Pediatric patients with ALGS	Open-label run-in with 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized withdrawal (RWD) period
The FDA focused on the 4-week RWD period comparing those who remained on maralixibat with those who switched to placebo.

population.text: Pediatric patients with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) with elevated serum bile acid levels (>3x the upper limit of normal for age).

citations.quote: LUM001-304 (NCT02160782)	Pediatric patients with ALGS	Open-label run-in with 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized withdrawal (RWD) period
Study LUM001-304 enrolled patients with elevated sBA levels (>3× the upper limit of normal [ULN] for age).

endpoint.text: The protocol-specified primary endpoint was mean change from Week 18 to 22 in fasting sBA level (in participants with sBA reduction >=50%); however sBA was not a validated surrogate, and effects on pruritus (ItchRO[Obs]) were secondary endpoints without a prespecified single primary pruritus endpoint, on which FDA based the efficacy conclusion.

citations.quote: Mean change from Week 18 to 22 of fasting sBA level in participants who had a reduction in sBA ≥50% from BL to Week 12 or 18

The primary endpoint specified in the protocol was based on the mean change in serum bile acids (sBAs). However, an effect on sBAs is not a validated surrogate endpoint that can be used to demonstrate clinical benefit. Effects on pruritus were secondary endpoints without a prespecified single primary pruritus endpoint.

n.text: 31 patients enrolled in the open-label run-in; 29 randomized to the RWD period (maralixibat 400 mcg/kg N=13; placebo N=16).

citations.quote: Study LUM001-304 was designed as a Phase 2 study and enrolled 31 patients with ALGS in an open-label study with a 4-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal period (RWD). Twenty-nine patients completed the open-label run-in period and were randomized to the RWD period as follows: Placebo arm N=16; maralixibat 400 mcg/kg arm N=13.

result.text: For the weekly average worst daily ItchRO(Obs) score, change from Week 18 to Week 22 was 0.2 (95% CI -0.3, 0.7) for maralixibat vs 1.6 (95% CI 1.2, 2.1) for placebo, mean treatment difference -1.4 (95% CI -2.1, -0.8), favoring continued maralixibat.

citations.quote: The mean (95% CI) change from Week 18 to Week 22 in the weekly average of the worst daily ItchRO(Obs) score for maralixibat was 0.2 (-0.3, 0.7) and placebo was 1.6 (1.2, 2.1), with a mean (95% CI) treatment difference of -1.4 (-2.1, -0.8).

indication.text: LIVMARLI is indicated for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) 1 year of age and older.

target_moa.text: Maralixibat is an inhibitor of the ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT); ~95% of bile acids are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum, and IBAT inhibition reduces reabsorption of bile salts, lowering serum bile acid levels.

citations.quote: Maralixibat is an inhibitor of the ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT). Bile acids (BAs) are synthesized from cholesterol in the liver. The primary function of BAs is to solubilize lipids into micelles, aiding digestion and absorption of fat and fat-soluble vitamins (FSV). Approximately 95% of the BAs secreted in the lumen of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum via

Maralixibat is an intestinal bile acid transport (IBAT) inhibitor that was granted Breakthrough Therapy designation for drug development as well as a Rare Pediatric Disease Designation for the treatment of pruritus associated with ALGS.

The Applicant was granted a rare pediatric disease designation from the Office of Orphan Products Development and the Office of Pediatric Therapeutics and met all criteria for receiving a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.
